2025 Interview Questions for a Data Engineering PySpark interview at Deloitte 👇

1. How would you package, configure, and deploy PySpark jobs for production use?
2. What’s your strategy for setting up efficient logging, alerting, and monitoring for PySpark pipelines?
3. How do you tune Spark executors, memory, and partitions to ensure balanced resource usage?
4. Write a PySpark job that aggregates daily transactions per customer from a large dataset.
5. How do you clean, impute, and validate inconsistent or incomplete data in PySpark DataFrames?
6. What’s your method to flatten multi-level nested JSON files into a relational format using PySpark?
7. If your PySpark transformation suffers from data skew, how do you detect and fix it?
8. When large joins lead to memory pressure, what optimization techniques would you apply?
9. Describe how you’d build a PySpark + Kafka pipeline to handle near real-time streaming data.
10. How would you detect unusual behavior in IoT or sensor streams using PySpark Structured Streaming?
11. How would you orchestrate a PySpark-based ETL job that extracts from SQL Server and loads into Snowflake?
12. What’s your approach to reading and transforming mixed-format data (CSV, Parquet, and JSON) in PySpark?
13. How do you merge external REST API data into your PySpark pipeline efficiently?
14. How would you join data coming from Hive tables and Kafka topics in a single PySpark job?
15. Describe how you’d handle schema evolution in streaming data with PySpark.

text:
⚠️ Data Engineers (2–5 YOE):
NTT DATA is NOT testing tools in 2025.
 They’re testing how you THINK.
I recently went through a real NTT DATA Data Engineer interview, and the pattern was crystal clear 👇
 If you miss this mindset, your interview won’t last long.
🔍 What NTT DATA actually asked (real scenarios):
✔️ “Explain an end-to-end data pipeline you built.”
 Not tools — architecture clarity (ADF → ADLS → Databricks → Delta → Synapse/Power BI).
✔️ “How do you avoid full loads?”
 Watermark-based incremental design + metadata-driven pipelines.
✔️ “What data quality checks do you implement?”
 Schema validation, null checks, business rules, rejection paths, auditability.
✔️ “Duplicates exist — keep only the latest record.”
 Window functions (row_number).
 GroupBy answers = rejected.
✔️ “Pipeline is slow. How do you optimize it?”
 Early filtering, column pruning, broadcast joins, repartitioning, AQE.
🚨 Interview Reality Check:
If your answers sound like:
 ❌ “We truncate and reload”
 ❌ “We rerun the pipeline”
 ❌ “Spark is fast by default”
You’re already filtered out.

author: Atharva Thakare
headline: Data Engineer @ TCS | Databricks • PySpark • SQL • Snowflake | AWS • Azure • Generative AI
text:
SQL Interview Questions for Data Engineers (Beginner → Advanced) 🚀

If you’re preparing for Data Engineering interviews, SQL is not optional — it’s your primary problem-solving tool.

Interviewers don’t just test syntax.
They test how well you think in data pipelines, transformations, and validations.

Here’s a structured breakdown 👇

🔹 Beginner Level (Foundations you must get right)

These test whether you understand how data is filtered and joined.

• Difference between WHERE vs HAVING
• INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL joins
• DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP
• PRIMARY KEY vs UNIQUE KEY
• Handling NULL values
• COUNT(*) vs COUNT(column)

👉 If you struggle here, advanced SQL won’t help.


🔹 Intermediate Level (Daily Data Engineering SQL)

This is where real transformation logic starts.

• What are window functions and why are they used?
• Difference between ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK
• How to find & remove duplicates
• CTEs vs Subqueries — when to use which
• CASE WHEN for business logic
• UNION vs UNION ALL

👉 Most ETL logic lives at this level.


🔹 Advanced Level (Data Engineering Core 🔥)

These questions separate query writers from data engineers.

• How do you implement SCD Type 1 & Type 2 in SQL?
• How do you design incremental loads?
• What is MERGE / UPSERT, and when do you use it?
• How do you compare source vs target data?
• How do you handle late-arriving data?
• Partitioning vs Indexing
• How do you analyze an execution plan?

👉 This is where interviewers decide your level.


🔹 Scenario-Based Questions (Most Important 💡)

These test real project experience.

• Source has 10M rows, target has 9.8M — how do you debug?
• How do you make pipelines idempotent?
• How do you safely reprocess data?
• What SQL checks do you add before production release?
• How do you ensure data quality after ETL?

👉 There is no single “correct” answer — only good reasoning.


🔹 Final Advice

❌ Don’t memorize queries
✅ Understand why the query exists in the pipeline

SQL for Data Engineers is about:

Data correctness

Performance

Business logic

Reproducibility


If you can explain your thinking, not just the syntax then you’ll clear interviews.

🚀 Monday Reality Check for Data Engineers (0–5 YOE)
Last Monday, a candidate told me:
“I know SQL, Spark, ADF… but the interview still went bad.”
He wasn’t rejected because he lacked tools.
 He was rejected because he didn’t prepare the right way.
Here’s what actually decides Data Engineer interviews 👇
📌 Interviewers don’t ask tools.
They test how you think under pressure.
So your preparation should look like this:
SQL
 → Can you explain why a query is slow, not just write it?
Spark / PySpark
 → Can you fix data skew at 2 AM when the job suddenly fails?
Data Warehousing
 → Can you choose the right SCD type when business changes rules?
ETL / ADF
 → Can you design an incremental load when the source has no timestamp?
Databricks / Delta
 → Can you stop performance degradation without adding more compute?
Streaming
 → Can you handle late data without breaking SLAs?
This is the gap most candidates miss.

headline: Sr. Data Engineer at Accenture Strategy |Ex-Deloitte, PwC | 3x Azure, 2x Databricks Certified | Transforming Data into Insights for Impact
text:
When I walked into my Persistent Systems 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄…..

I thought they’d ask basic questions like 𝗣𝘆𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗦𝘆𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘅 𝗼𝗿 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗷𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘀.

I had spent weeks revising:- 
 - SQL queries.
 - PySpark syntax. 
 - Window functions. 

Basically, everything people assume matters when switching into Data Engineering. 

𝗜 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲:
 • Write a query to find duplicate records.
 • Explain how #Spark handles lazy evaluation.

𝗕𝘂𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗱, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗲𝗱: 

Your #ETL jobs take 8 hours and delay downstream reports. 
How would you redesign the pipeline to reduce processing time? 

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁’𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗶𝘁 𝗵𝗶𝘁 𝗺𝗲: 
- Data Engineering interviews are NOT memory tests. 
- They don’t care if you’ve memorized every Spark feature. 

They care if you can: 

- Make systems faster 
- Reduce costs 
- Build pipelines that don’t break under pressure 

Because anyone can write #SQL. 
But only a true Data Engineer can fix a failing pipeline. ✅ 

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 Persistent Systems 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗸𝘀 𝗙𝗼𝗿:
It’s not about listing tools. It’s about showing that you can:-

✅ Design resilient, scalable systems 
✅ Make thoughtful, real-world decisions 
✅ Translate tech into business impact

If you can explain why you made a choice not just how — you’re already ahead.

This experience taught me that top-tier interviews are about engineering mindset, not just technical recall.
